headline: High Arctic Expedition Registration and Safety
reservation: Aulavik is one of the most remote parks in Canada; mandatory orientation and registration with Parks Canada in Inuvik or Sachs Harbour is required before departure. Permits for backcountry camping are managed through the Parks Canada Western Arctic office. Flight charter availability is the primary bottleneck and should be confirmed months in advance.

days.title: Thomsen River Lowlands
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Muskox Way landing

stops.name: Thomsen River
stops.detail: Paddle the northernmost navigable river in North America, observing the lush arctic oasis in the desert-like environment.

stops.name: Castel Bay
stops.detail: Hike the coastal bluffs where the river meets the McClure Strait, keeping watch for marine wildlife.

days.driving: Allow 3–5 hours for river transit; current speeds vary by seasonal melt.
days.note: River levels fluctuate based on upstream snowmelt and can impact paddling speed.

days.title: Ancient Arctic History

stops.name: Head Hill
stops.detail: Visit this significant archaeological site featuring muskox skulls and evidence of ancient Thule and Inuit occupation.

stops.name: Green Cabin
stops.detail: Utilize this historic waypoint as a base for exploring the surrounding muskox grazing meadows.

days.driving: Travel is entirely by foot or non-motorized watercraft; terrain is uneven tundra.
days.note: High concentrations of muskox require maintaining official wildlife viewing distances.

days.title: Banks Island Interior
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Green Cabin area

stops.name: Mercy Bay
stops.detail: Explore the site associated with the HMS Investigator and the search for the Northwest Passage.

stops.name: Tundra Plateau
stops.detail: Hike the interior plateaus for a perspective on the vast, treeless 'Great Land' of the Inuvialuit.

days.driving: Allow for a flexible charter pick-up window; weather frequently delays Arctic flights.
days.note: Persistent summer daylight allows for flexible hiking hours, but wind chill remains a factor.

intel.title: Charter Logic
intel.text: Access requires a Twin Otter charter from Inuvik, approximately 750km away. Visitors must coordinate with the few authorized air carriers serving Banks Island.

intel.title: Complete Isolation
intel.text: There is no cellular or internet service within the park. Satellite phones and PLBs are mandatory for all independent expeditions for safety reporting.

intel.title: Self-Sufficiency
intel.text: All stove fuel and food must be flown in from Inuvik. There are no stores or refueling points on Banks Island outside the small community of Sachs Harbour.

intel.title: Arctic Window
intel.text: The travel season is restricted to July and August. Ice break-up on the Thomsen River usually occurs in late June, and winter conditions return rapidly in September.

intel.title: Non-Applicable
intel.text: There are no roads or parking facilities in Aulavik. Vehicle logistics are limited to airport transfers in Inuvik or quad-trailer transport in Sachs Harbour.

plan.arrival: Arrive in Inuvik via YEV, attend the mandatory Parks Canada safety briefing, and finalize your Twin Otter charter weight limits before heading to the floatplane base.
plan.vehicle: No vehicles are used within the park; transport is exclusively by specialized charter aircraft and watercraft.
plan.goldenHour: The 'Midnight Sun' at Castel Bay, where the sun skims the horizon without setting during the height of summer.
